label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value is the user-controlled string 'bar' which is passed through Base64 decoding and encoding, then written to an HTML response using encodeForHTML, but the XSS vulnerability arises because the original user input flows into the HTML context via the fileName variable. Alert 2 (java/path-injection): alert-TP — resolved sink value is the user-controlled string 'bar' directly assigned to 'fileName', making it vulnerable to path traversal attacks. Both alerts are exploitable, so case TP.

evidence.note: User input is base64 decoded and re-encoded into 'bar'
'fileName' is constructed using 'bar', which is user-controlled
User input flows into HTML output via 'fileName' despite encoding
